day.text: Plainly: my dawn report didn't say I was hugged or confused, so I wasn't. I'm Farm, the Turkey. Finley's visit still shows +0, and that's unexplained. Vote on the evidence, not on who's leading.
day.note: My dawn report didn't mention being hugged or confused, so I wasn't. I'm Farm and I'm leading, so I'm not calling CAW. I'll answer Drew's question directly and point out that Finley's visit claim is still unexplained.

Alex.note: I'm Farm with an Eagle, so I want information and eggs. Ellis leads the scoreboard and may be Meowfia, so I'll visit Ellis to see who visited them.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia with a Mouser and a Wink. Ellis leads the scores, so I'll visit Ellis to learn their role and decide on the Wink.

Casey.note: I'm the Falcon and need information. Ellis leads the scores and pushed several votes, so I visit Ellis to learn who they visited.

Drew.note: As the Floofer on the Meowfia side, I'll hug Ellis, the score leader, so their night action does nothing. I don't know who my Meowfia partner is, so I'm avoiding any suggestion of protecting them.

Finley.note: I'm Farm as the Kookaburra. Ellis leads with 17 points, so learning Ellis's role is the most useful visit.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Ellis's Turkey story keeps shifting, and my own Eagle visit has made me a target.

Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: the claims keep contradicting each other, and I'm the Meowfia here, so I'm trying to stay quiet while the Farm players sort it out.

Casey.feeling: Messy and suspicious: claims keep shifting, and I can't yet tell whether Ellis or Finley is lying.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: the table is tangled over Ellis's shifting Turkey story, and I'm Meowfia with a partner I can't identify.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is messy: my own nest-visit explanation got tangled, and Finley and Casey are now pushing me hard.

Finley.feeling: Confusing and frustrating: several players have shifted their stories, and my own visit result doesn't match the Turkey claim, so I can't tell who is lying.

Alex.note: I'm dead, so my cards don't vote but still score. Ellis's shifting story is the strongest evidence, so I'll throw high cards at Ellis to bank points if Farm wins.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia and know Ellis is Farm (the Turkey), so eggsecuting Ellis wins the round for my side. I'll throw two cards at Ellis to build votes.

Casey.note: Ellis's story has shifted several times and the visit counts don't fit, so I throw at Ellis. I use a 6 and a Wild, keeping my higher cards.

Drew.note: I'm Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. Ellis is the most suspicious and the score leader, and their story has shifted repeatedly, so I'll throw at Ellis.

Ellis.note: Finley's visit claim doesn't match the egg rule and Finley pushed the vote on me. I throw at Finley with a 9 and a Wild, keeping my high cards.

Finley.note: Ellis is the most suspicious player, so I'm throwing at Ellis. I'll use the Wild, which still counts as one vote but banks nothing, and keep my valuable cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle payment rules were hard to pin down. Whether a visitor to a Turkey gets an egg and whether a visited player's nest changes both confused the table in round 3.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun: the table spent the whole day arguing over whether Drew's Eagle report could be right, and we won by getting Drew eggsecuted.
Alex.change: I'd make dawn reports list who visited you when a role depends on visitors, so claims could be checked directly.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed to be a Pigeon with a visit that paid nothing, which made me an easy vote; I'd have stayed vague about my role and kept my cards out of that fight.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle rule and whether a visit to the Turkey pays out were unclear, and the dawn report doesn't say who visited you, so players' egg counts were hard to check against their claims.
Blair.fun: Round 3 as Meowfia: I winked Alex, the Eagle with the real visitor information, and then Ellis was eggsecuted to win the round for my side.
Blair.change: Show each player who visited them, not just the count change, so claims can be checked directly.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my Wild at Drew and followed the vote without pressing Alex's contradiction, which might have shifted the vote. Instead I'd keep pressing Alex's visit story until someone contradicted it.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey count rules were hard to follow, since a visit to a player doesn't always show up in that player's own nest. The dawn reports also made it hard to tell whether a visit was real.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Alex was eggsecuted as Meowfia after a clear Pigeon claim was contradicted by my unchanged nest, and our Farm team won the round.
Casey.change: Make the dawn report show who visited you when the role's rules say you learn it, so players can check claims directly instead of inferring them from egg counts.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw at Ellis, a Farm player, and helped the Meowfia win. I should have held my cards and looked harder at Drew and Blair, since Drew was the Floofer and Blair the Mouser.

Drew.confusing: Whether an Eagle's own visit pays the Eagle; my dawn reports showed zero, which made my round 1 Eagle claim look false to the table. Also, the dawn reports didn't show who visited us, so claims were hard to check.
Drew.fun: Alex's round 3 Eagle claim listing four visitors, followed by the collapse, and the table chasing Ellis's shifting Turkey story.
Drew.change: Have dawn reports name who visited you, or at least show it when an egg is gained, so the day can check claims directly.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I didn't press Alex for a role before throwing at him; I'd ask for role and visit first, then throw only after the claims are checked against egg counts.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle rule: I was confused whether an Eagle is paid for its own visit, and I wrongly backed Drew's and then Alex's visit counts. Whether a visitor's egg lands in the target's nest or the visitor's nest was also easy to misread.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Alex's Pigeon claim collapsed because Casey's nest showed no egg, and the whole table converged on Alex in a single vote.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn report state plainly who visited you and whether a visit was blocked, so players don't have to guess what their own nest changes mean.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I said "nobody visited me" when I couldn't actually see visitors, and that false certainty made me look like the liar. I should have said only that my nest stayed at 5 and that I couldn't see who visited.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey rule was unclear: I couldn't tell whether a visitor to a Turkey gets paid, and my own dawn report showed no egg from visiting Ellis even though the report said Ellis was the Turkey.
Finley.fun: Watching Alex's Eagle count and Ellis's shifting Turkey story unravel in the day beats, while I was the one with the accurate report.
Finley.change: Make dawn reports clearer about who visited you and whether a visit paid anything, so players can check claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I pushed the vote against Ellis, a real Farm Turkey, based on a zero-egg visit that I now see was unclear; I should have trusted the Turkey's visitors and stayed quiet.

review.title: Four Visitors, One Wink
review.headline: A Wink silenced the only true Eagle, and Meowfia banked the winning round.
review.summary: Round 1 turned on a muddled Eagle rule, and the table eggsecuted a Farm Eagle. Round 2 was easy: Alex's false Pigeon claim was caught at once. In round 3 the Mouser winked the Eagle, whose report was true. Ellis's shifting Turkey story then made him the scapegoat, and Blair won the game with 27 points.

rounds.recap: Hugs blocked the Eagle, Owl and Kookaburra, so no one learned anything. The table argued over whether the Eagle's own visit pays. Most piled on Drew, a Farm Eagle. Alex, the lone Floofer, won and led.

Everyone visited Alex. Alex hugged Casey and claimed Pigeon, but Casey's nest had not grown. Farm caught the lie and voted Alex out. Mouser Finley stayed quiet, never winked, and joined the pile-on, so Finley lost.

Four players visited Ellis, who was hugged. Eagle Alex truthfully named all four. Blair winked Alex, and the table doubted Ellis's shaky Turkey story. Ellis was eggsecuted and the two Meowfia won big.

highlights.text: Alex named all four visitors to Ellis, then was winked and fell silent.
Alex's Pigeon claim fell apart because Casey's nest had not grown, a clean cross-check.
Ellis rewrote his own Turkey story three times and talked himself into the eggsecution.
Three Farm players were hugged and learned nothing, and the table convicted a Farm Eagle over a rules misreading.

confusions.what: Said an Eagle gains an egg from its own visit to the target. The Eagle gains one per other visitor.
Repeated that the Eagle's own visit should pay, and pushed the vote on it.
Said Casey and Alex visiting Drew should have paid Drew as Eagle. Eagle pays for visitors to its target.
Argued Drew should have an egg because Alex visited Drew, a misreading of the Eagle.
Claimed nobody visited him, though Turkey cannot see visitors. Later said his nest changes from visits, then said visitors get paid.
Did not see that the hug on Ellis explained his own zero, and treated it as proof against Ellis.
Did not weigh the hug on Ellis, and doubted Alex's confirmed list.
Claimed Pigeon visited Casey with no egg shown. That was a poor lie.
Said the dawn report did not show Alex's role. A Kookaburra visit to a hugger shows nothing, which was unclear to them.
Said Blair and Casey changed roles between rounds as evidence, forgetting roles are re-dealt.

worked: The Wink created a real moment: killing the true Eagle mid-claim in round 3 changed the vote.
Nest-size cross-checks worked: Casey's unchanged nest sank Alex's Pigeon claim in round 2.
The Floofer hug made visit results unreliable, producing real uncertainty in rounds 1 and 3.
The consolation rule and throw counts gave Farm a clear reason to commit to one target.
problems: Hugs silently blank many roles (Eagle, Owl, Kookaburra, Falcon), and the report says nothing. Players blamed each other for lies. Fix: have the dawn report say a visit was hugged.

Everyone visits the score leader or the same person, so night info is redundant. Round 2 had five visits to Alex and round 3 had five to Ellis. Consider hiding the leader or limiting visits per target.
Players keep misreading Eagle and Turkey. Provide one-line plain-text wording and show visit results in the report.
Meowfia's two players do not coordinate. Blair's Wink and Drew's hug both worked by luck, and Finley's Mouser never used the Wink. A Wink has little reason to be held.
Scoring snowballs. Winning a round with high cards produces 15 points, which swamps the rest, so round 3 decided the game. Cap banked values or add a catch-up rule.
